why: Stage 9b rewrote notes for plain words. A rewrite is a new note and carries the same risk as the one it replaced, so every one is read blind, as repairs are.

instruments.author: .claude/agents/simplifier.md
instruments.rule: census-reader.md unchanged from censuses 007-012: the reader measures truth, not ease, so this rate compares with theirs; the instrument gate must pass before grading

stop_condition: over 5% stops the pass: it means simplifying is changing meaning, a method problem before a batch one
read_design: complete read of every rewrite; census_packets.py slices contiguously; reader sees gloss, charge label and note, never the old note or that it was rewritten

entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds too much like a word from a book to hurt - its strangeness softens the greed into something funny.

entries.definition: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-y* ending makes the pig little - small enough to carry no real anger.
examples: the piggy fat-cheeked little boy and his porcine pot-bellied father

entries.definition: capable of being reached or attained
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same informal word written as one lump, clumsier on the page than *get-at-able* and no different in force.
examples: both oil and coal are there but not in getatable locations

entries.definition: easily approached
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and literal where *approachable* is inviting: it notes the ease and adds nothing to it.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs what is brought against what the task needs and finds a mismatch, where *inadequate* calls the lack a fault in the thing.
examples: she was unequal to the task

entries.definition: giving an advantage
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, calculating approval: it weighs only the edge a thing gives you, not whether that edge is deserved or does any good.
examples: a contract advantageous to our country

entries.definition: manifesting partiality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusing where its neighbours approve - it treats favouring one side as the wrong itself, not as a favour worth having.

entries.definition: (used in combination) affected by something overwhelming
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Added to another word, its blow lands like a spell: softer-sounding than *stricken*, but just as total.

entries.definition: likely to be affected by something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names exposure, not outcome: nothing has landed yet, the thing just stands open to it, unlike every struck-and-overcome word here.
examples: the bond is subject to taxation
he is subject to fits of depression

entries.definition: a mistake that results from taking one thing to be another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names how it happened - one thing taken for another - which lets the mistake sound explainable rather than someone's fault.
examples: he changed his name in order to avoid confusion with the notorious outlaw

entries.definition: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cool: it notes the reaching for recognition or advancement without judging it, where *aspiring* sounds warm.

entries.definition: full of spirit; full of life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More formal than *lively* and carrying more weight: the same fullness of life, sounding like a force inside, not liveliness on show.

entries.definition: expressing yourself readily, clearly, effectively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves of how the words come out - without friction - and is a plainer word than *eloquent*.

entries.definition: speaking or spoken fittingly or pleasingly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves speech that fits the occasion or pleases the ear, where *fluent* asks only that the words come easily.
examples: a few well-spoken words on civic pride

entries.definition: feeling shame or guilt or embarrassment or remorse
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for the feeling, wide enough for guilt and remorse as well as shame; unlike *disgraced*, it says nothing about reputation.
examples: are you ashamed for having lied?
felt ashamed of my torn coat

entries.definition: showing a sense of guilt
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful, and it paints a picture: guilt shown as a shrinking, beaten posture, and the word enjoys saying so.
examples: the hangdog and shamefaced air of the retreating enemy

entries.definition: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Where *mortified* measures how sharp the discomfort is, this measures how far down it puts a person, through shame or wounded pride.
examples: humiliated that his wife had to go out to work

entries.definition: mentally perceptive and responsive
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shows a sharp, noticing mind as full of life - stirred and answering, rather than simply watchful.
examples: alive to what is going on

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-ed* form turns it around: the thing is defined by the dread already aimed at it, where *dreadful* says it causes dread.
examples: polio is no longer the dreaded disease it once was

entries.definition: (superlative of ‘good’) having the most positive qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The highest form itself - it ends the comparison rather than making one.
examples: the best film of the year

entries.definition: having or covered with or accompanied by blood
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for blood in a thing, on it, or simply alongside it, and it judges none of these.
examples: the effects will be violent and probably bloody

entries.definition: accompanied by bloodshed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts a butcher's hand on the bloodshed - crude, like a day's work, and scornful of whoever did it, where *slaughterous* is merely grand.

entries.definition: characteristic of or capable of or having a tendency toward killing another human being
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical in tone and wide in reach: it covers a settled tendency to kill, the bare ability, and what is typical of killing.

entries.definition: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and its cool tone sits strangely on an eagerness for bloodshed, condemning from a distance where *bloodthirsty* condemns close up.
examples: went after the collaborators with a sanguinary fury that drenched the land with blood

entries.definition: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Its *un-* means not a ripple raised, so it hints at water that held its surface, where *smooth* just describes one.

entries.definition: without or almost without wind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare measure - no wind, or almost none - without the approval *tranquil* carries.
examples: he prefers windless days for playing golf

entries.definition: developed or executed with care and in minute detail
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The *-ed* form, cooler than *elaborate*: it marks a thing as having been worked out rather than admiring the result.

entries.definition: excessively or unduly careful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunter than *overcareful*: 'too' spells out the excess in plain words, where *overcareful* tucks it into the front of the word.

entries.definition: marked by excessive confidence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest word for too much confidence: an everyday word that lets the excess come across as a shrug, not an accusation.
examples: the less he knows, the more positive he gets

entries.definition: having confidence restored; freed from anxiety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The settled calm of confidence handed back as worry lifts, where the rest of the family never mentions it having been shaken.
examples: reassured by her praise he pressed on

entries.definition: causing dejection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and it colours the mood without condemning the thing, where *dismal* passes judgement on it.

entries.definition: causing dejection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Lowers the spirits in a small, stale way: too minor for the wide reach of *dismal*, but enough to bring a mood down.

entries.definition: causing dejection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gloom from dull sameness: it makes a mood flat rather than dark, lowering the spirits without the threat of *grim*.

entries.definition: causing dejection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain middle of the family: it names the low spirits it causes without making them stronger, where *dismal* passes judgement.

entries.definition: causing dejection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gloom mixed with scorn: what it names is not just depressing but pathetic, which *gloomy* never suggests.

entries.definition: causing sad feelings of gloom and inadequacy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of these - just 'not cheerful', noting the missing cheer without the settled bleakness *cheerless* carries.

entries.definition: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical - a softer word, chosen to avoid saying *dirty*.

entries.definition: readily apparent to the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word: a thing reaches the mind without effort, and it does not say whether that is a good thing.
examples: a clear indication that she was angry
gave us a clear idea of human nature

entries.definition: marked by practical hardheaded intelligence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal praise for judgement that sees through a situation, carrying more weight than *sharp*, which praises speed instead.
examples: an astute tenant always reads the small print in a lease

entries.definition: suggesting connivance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling of *cozy*, with the same accusation of secret cooperation in wrongdoing - warmth named in order to be distrusted.

entries.definition: suggesting connivance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hints at wrongdoing - the closeness is treated as secret cooperation, so the word's comfortable warmth becomes the accusation.
examples: a cozy arrangement with the police

entries.definition: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a place for feeling like home and putting you at ease, where *cozy* praises its warmth.

entries.definition: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The informal version of *bad*, looser and more casual about the same felt discomfort.
examples: he was feeling tough after a restless night

entries.definition: providing or experiencing physical discomfort
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain general word, fitting both the thing that causes discomfort and the body that feels it, which keeps it flat.
examples: an uncomfortable day in the hot sun

entries.definition: uncomfortable because of possible danger or trouble
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Places the discomfort in possible danger or trouble, not in the body, and its mildness is what makes it sound like a warning.
examples: made things warm for the bookies

entries.definition: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest approval here: it sets a minimum and says it was met - qualified, capable or efficient enough, and no more.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavy and sternly critical - it treats the behaviour as a failure of judgement serious enough to name, where *craziness* simply calls it mad.
examples: Follies and nonsense, whims and inconsistencies, do divert me, I own, and I laugh at them whenever I can.
to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others

entries.definition: acting like a clown or buffoon
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at clowning and playing the fool - silly performance rather than the bad judgement *folly* names, so the disapproval comes with amusement.

entries.definition: serenely self-possessed and free from agitation especially in times of stress
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of calm kept up on purpose while the pressure is on, not the luck of an easy hour.
examples: the performer seemed completely composed as she stepped onto the stage
I felt calm and more composed than I had in a long time

entries.definition: not agitated; without losing self-possession
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly descriptive: it notes that agitation is absent, without giving anyone credit for holding it off.

entries.definition: impossible to determine the meaning of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the thing as a code that cannot be cracked: you are beaten by the meaning, not the style as with *obscure*.

entries.definition: difficult to understand
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Has exactly the force of *incomprehensible* but sounds put together on the spot, its un- plainer than the in-.

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-ing* form keeps the careless speed going on as an activity, not the single finished act *rush* names.

entries.definition: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The undignified hurry as a clumsy, messy struggle, where *scamper* is just quick and silly.

entries.definition: not compatible with other facts
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and measuring - it notes the mismatch with the facts coolly, where *incompatible* passes judgement on it.

entries.definition: lacking consistency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of these - it notes variation without deciding that any part of the thing has failed.

entries.definition: constant and unchanging
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute and cool: it states that a thing does not change, without the praise for holding firm that *steadfast* carries.

entries.definition: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heavier than *constant*, because it adds being reliable: the firmness becomes something others can lean on.

entries.definition: tireless
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Tireless like *unfailing*, but pictured as a pace that never slows rather than a supply that never runs out.

entries.definition: based on interpretation; not directly expressed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no approval - it says how something is reached, by interpretation, not statement, where *constructive* judges the worth of what is done.

entries.definition: helping to restore to good condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same approving sense of repair as *reconstructive*, but the longer, more formal word makes the help sound ongoing, not a single fix.

entries.definition: showing or experiencing dissatisfaction or restless longing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Covers dissatisfaction or restless longing like *discontented*, but reads as a fixed state where *discontented* allows a passing mood.
examples: saw many discontent faces in the room

entries.definition: in a state of sulky dissatisfaction
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes light of the complaint - the grumpy tone turns it into a mere mood, brushed aside along with the person complaining.

entries.definition: lacking spontaneity or originality or individuality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Everyday and scornful - the thing is so easy to guess that you can see it coming.

entries.definition: rigidly conventional or old-fashioned
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat slang for the same stiff or old-fashioned ways, naming rather than mocking, so it lands softer than *square*.

entries.definition: pertaining to unconventional choices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the break from the usual as something chosen, and a choice can be described without being condemned.

entries.definition: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dismissive — the strangeness is treated as too lightweight to be taken seriously.

entries.definition: having a body or a body of a specified kind; often used in combination
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral base of the set: just a body, or a body of whatever kind the word before it names.

entries.definition: having a relatively long body
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pure measurement in one direction - long compared with other bodies, with no praise or fault in it.

entries.definition: having a silver-colored body
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The -y ending softens the colour to 'like silver' - a sheen hinted at where *silver-bodied* names the shade outright.

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval at its lowest: it grants only that the manner was not rude, where *polite* can stretch to social rules kept well enough.
examples: even if he didn't like them he should have been civil
Mr. Bingley was unaffectedly civil in his answer, and forced his younger sister to be civil also
It was more than civil; it was really attentive

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the social rules as kept, not merely rudeness avoided.

entries.definition: bewildering or striking dumb with wonder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heaviest impact here, falling on the person instead of rating the claim: thrown into confusion or struck silent with wonder.

entries.definition: barely credible
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Leaves the thing only just believable, where *incredible* puts it past belief, and the stretch sounds like extravagance, not a fault.
examples: the fabulous endurance of a marathon runner

entries.definition: beyond belief or understanding
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the thing wholly past belief or understanding, not just very unlikely, and says nothing of whether that is wonderful or awful.
examples: the book's plot is simply incredible

entries.definition: being in or verging on a state of crisis or emergency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Marks the tipping point, the moment things break one way or the other - cooler and more clinical than *grave*.
examples: an illness at the critical stage

entries.definition: causing fear or anxiety by threatening great harm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest word here: it insists the threatened harm is real, without making its force dramatic as *severe* does.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Leans hardest here on the very positive use: the trait does not just identify the thing, it raises it above others.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Notes the trait as a sign the thing carries, crediting it lightly where *distinguish* lifts it.
examples: there is that in her features which marks the young woman of distinguished birth
every sentence of her uncle, which marked his intelligence, his taste, or his good manners

entries.definition: eager to investigate and learn or learn more (sometimes about others' concerns)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves of the eager mind, a little wary of the manner - the meaning allows both.
examples: a curious child is a teacher's delight
a trap door that made me curious
traffic was slowed by curious rubberneckers

entries.definition: not current or belonging to the present time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest word here - it simply says something does not belong to the present, without the judgement *obsolete* passes.

entries.definition: damaged by blows or hard usage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal where *battered* is not, treating the same hard usage as something to shrug at rather than record.

entries.definition: in deplorable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Wears its awful state on the surface, so it invites pity rather than shame, where *derelict* makes it a matter for blame.

entries.definition: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Only says the thing does not work - not how it got that way, which is nearly all *battered* tells you.

entries.definition: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The informal word for *broken*, and the casual tone makes the same failure sound offhand rather than serious.

entries.definition: of metal e.g.
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Damage to the shape across the whole thing, not along one line - more thorough than *bent*, but judging just as little.
examples: a car with a crumpled front end

entries.definition: accept as true
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and informal where *believe* is plain: it treats a claim as something on offer, so accepting it sounds weighed, not simply held.
examples: He says the delay was the weather's fault, but I don't buy that.

entries.definition: believe or accept without questioning or challenge
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Looks down on the believer, not the claim: to swallow something is to accept it without question or challenge.
examples: Am I supposed to swallow that story?

entries.definition: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shows disgust rather than disapproval: the thing is so coarse it makes you feel sick, and the word itself is the shudder.

entries.definition: verging on the indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest criticism here - close to indecent but not quite there, so it scolds where *obscene* accuses.

entries.definition: determining or having the power to determine an outcome
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word, covering what settles an outcome and what only has the power to, with no view on how it turns out.
examples: two factors had a decisive influence

entries.definition: have faith or confidence in
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the faith as a stake laid down, admitting in the same breath that it could be lost, which *rely* never does.

entries.definition: put trust in with confidence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Settled, nothing held back: the trust is already placed and resting there, with none of the risk still heard in *bet*.

entries.definition: brought low in spirit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Same sense as *chopfallen*, and like it stresses the fall: a spirit brought down from a height, not one always low.

entries.definition: filled with melancholy and despondency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the loss rather than the mood - the spirit has been drained out, which comes across as emptiness beside *gloomy*'s heaviness.
examples: a dispirited and resigned expression on her face

entries.definition: filled with melancholy and despondency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, with a little dry humour - it points at a turned-down mouth, not the feeling, making the state sound smaller than it is.

entries.definition: filled with melancholy and despondency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gentle and sympathetic, placing the low spirits in the heart and inviting comfort where *grim* rules it out.

entries.definition: filled with melancholy and despondency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Spreads rather than strikes - the low, hopeless mood hangs around the person like settled weather, where *deflated* feels like one blow.
examples: gloomy at the thought of what he had to face

entries.definition: requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and calm - it names how much is asked without judging whether that is fair, where *hard-to-please* has already found someone guilty.
examples: a baby can be so demanding

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - the strictness comes across as discipline worth having, where *tight* only pinches.

entries.definition: capable of arousing sexual desire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Enjoys the sexual desire the thing stirs, where the cooler *sexually attractive* only reports it.

entries.definition: more desirable than another
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A comparison and nothing more - it rates one thing above another without claiming either is wanted much at all.

entries.definition: destroyed financially
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Financial ruin in the bluntest word: a single snap rather than a decline, with no blame on the one it fell on.
examples: the broken fortunes of the family

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches from scorched to gone: it names fire as the cause but leaves open how much survives, where *burned-out* pins that down.
examples: a burned-over site in the forest

entries.definition: destroyed or badly damaged by fire
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The shorter form reads as a state the thing is now in, where *burned* reports what happened to it.
examples: a charred bit of burnt wood
barricaded the street with burnt-out cars

entries.definition: spoiled or ruined or demolished
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Stretches from merely spoiled to flattened: it says ruin happened but not how much is left, where *annihilated* leaves nothing.
examples: Alzheimer's is responsible for her destroyed mind

entries.definition: destroyed completely
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Has a purpose *annihilated* lacks: somebody did it, and the word treats what was destroyed as a thing to get rid of.

entries.definition: destroyed financially
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, naming the poverty left behind rather than the break itself - a settled state, where *broken* sounds like a moment.

entries.definition: reduced to nothingness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare form, without *-ed*, says flatly that nothing is left, with no look back at what caused it, which *obliterated* keeps.

entries.definition: reduced to nothingness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cold beside *blotted out*: the *-ed* ending points back to an act, and nothing is left, not something hidden.

entries.definition: affected by blight; anything that mars or prevents growth or prosperity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling, and milder: the good has gone out of it, where *blighted* adds that nothing will come of it now.

entries.definition: morally objectionable behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the same conduct with preachy relish, as if the wrong were knowingly enjoyed, not just done: more vivid than the bare *evil*.

entries.definition: difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty - it stresses the long mental effort and skill needed to get the thing done, a heavier word than *hard*.
examples: the arduous work of preparing a dictionary

entries.definition: having concealed difficulty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Warns of a trap - the difficulty stays hidden until you are into it, so the thing is harder than it looks.

entries.definition: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns the demand on everything you have into an invitation to rise to it, where *problematic* treats the demand as a fault.
examples: performed the most challenging task without a mistake

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unemotional - it states the thing takes effort to do, grasp or bear, without *challenging*'s hint that the effort is worth it.
examples: nesting places on the cliffs are difficult of access

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blunt, plain-spoken version of *difficult*, taking effort of body, mind or endurance as it comes and softening none of it.
examples: why is it so hard for you to keep a secret?

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal - you are caught in the trouble and cannot step cleanly out, lighter in tone than *unenviable* but no easier to escape.

entries.definition: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A charge of deliberate faking or of overdoing it, so the fault is excess as much as falseness.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest word here for faking it: the fault is the wish to look good, where *pretence* blames the falseness itself.
examples: he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right

entries.definition: the act of giving a false appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, general word for putting up a false front, without the wish to impress that softens *appearance*; British spelling.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sees the same pretending to impress as an act put on for an audience, with more scorn for the performance than *appearance* has.
examples: that ceremony is just for show

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for hostility at a wrong that may be real or only supposed, so the blame lands lighter than in *wrath*.
examples: Anger is counted among the seven deadly sins.

entries.definition: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns while it defines: a shameful greed for getting things, and a hunger for wealth that nothing can fill.

entries.definition: spite and resentment at seeing the success of another (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not simply wanting what another has: spite and resentment at their success are the meaning itself.

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same hostility raised to solemn weight: a word sized for a sin, where *anger* is sized for a mood.

entries.definition: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A flat accusation: the swollen self-esteem of *pride* turned outward, as an overbearing, superior manner toward those it looks down on.

entries.definition: unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Here a fault, not a virtue: self-esteem grown too big and past all reason, serious enough to be one of the deadly sins.
examples: Everybody is disgusted with his pride.
They had nothing to accuse him of but pride

entries.definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pleading at its most formal - an appeal made from a humble stance rather than *beg*'s bare asking.
examples: Pray forgive me, if I have been very presuming
and pray tell her from me, that she cannot expect to excel, if she does not practise a great deal

entries.definition: having or showing appreciation or a favorable critical judgment or opinion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm rather than cool: it names plain appreciation or a favourable judgment, where *discriminating* says only that the judgment is sharp.
examples: an appreciative laugh from the audience

entries.definition: able to make or detect effects of great subtlety; sensitive
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a perception fine enough to make and catch effects too subtle for a duller eye, where *selective* only picks among the obvious.

entries.definition: easy to perceive; especially clearly outlined
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain starting point here: something can be told apart, with no claim about how fine or admirable its edge is.
examples: the ship appeared as a distinct silhouette

entries.definition: very clearly delineated
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Clearness of outline taken as far as it goes, next to which *sharp* sounds just good enough.

entries.definition: lure by imitating the characteristic call of an animal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and technical: the lure is an imitated animal cry, so all the trickery is in the sound, none in any promise.

entries.definition: entice and trap
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Enticing is only half of it - the trap closing is the other half, and that makes it land harder than *entice*.

entries.definition: painful as if caused by a sharp instrument
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The *-ing* twin of *lancinate*, just as clinical, but the pain is still going on as it is described.

entries.definition: full of life and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain starting point: life and energy with no image attached, so every other word here colours it in some way.

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same flash said in a smaller, prettier way - decorative where *scintillating* is dazzling.

entries.definition: highly educated; having extensive information or understanding
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the sheer amount someone knows - everyday and plain, where *learned* is solemn.

entries.definition: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and accusing: it blames the person for not knowing a field's basics, where *untutored* blames a lack of schooling.
examples: she is ignorant of quantum mechanics
He is ignorant of chemistry and could not read the label.

entries.definition: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the full force of 'cannot read' on one field's basics, so a limited gap sounds total - showier scorn than *ignorant*.

entries.definition: lacking knowledge gained by study often in a particular field
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat report that knowledge was not gained by study, in a field or in general, with none of *ignorant*'s blame.
examples: is unstudied in Latin as he is in may other matters

entries.definition: lacking in schooling
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild, almost taking the blame off the person: the lack is in the schooling they never had, not in their mind.

entries.definition: act as an informer
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the act a role: you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the role carries a faint stain *tell* lacks.
examples: He informed on his own brother to the police.

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Only says something was made bigger; the fault is in going too far, not the word, so it accuses least of the three.

entries.definition: cause someone to believe an untruth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same planting of a false belief as *deceive*, but seen as breaking the trust that made the believing possible.

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain accusation of overstating - past reasonable limits or past the truth - always implying the real size is smaller.
examples: tended to romanticize and exaggerate this ‘gracious Old South’ imagery

entries.definition: morally binding or necessary
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and serious: it ties the duty to whoever it rests on, where *mandatory* states it as a general rule.
examples: it is incumbent on me to attend

entries.definition: pretentiously elegant
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scorns the elegance as put on - the height is only for show.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Crisp and practical - the pace wins approval for its efficiency alone, with none of the lightness *merry* adds.
examples: a brisk walk in the park

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More emphasis than description, pushing quickness toward a flat-out rush in a way *brisk* never does.

entries.definition: having or showing great excitement and interest
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word: it reports the excitement and interest without judging whether they are deserved, the very thing *overenthusiastic* judges.
examples: was enthusiastic about taking ballet lessons

entries.definition: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a contest or its contestants, it blames the pairing itself: these two should never have been set against each other.

entries.definition: not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity, or significance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat denial, not a complaint: the two are not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity or significance.

entries.definition: having a better than even chance of success
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The only word here where the imbalance is good news: a better than even chance of success, an advantage rather than a fault.

entries.definition: not caused to be equal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at what was not done - nothing has been made equal - where *unequal* judges the gap that remains.

entries.definition: indicate by marking trees with blazes
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Literal where *mark* is not: the sign is really cut into trees, so the word names its method and judges nothing.

entries.definition: make conspicuous or noteworthy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The only one here that lifts the thing up, making it stand out or worth noticing, where *mark* just labels it.
examples: Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters.
with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth

entries.definition: completely wanting or lacking
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light and quietly joking - a complete lack made to sound free of blame, the opposite feeling from *destitute*.

entries.definition: nonexistent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the absence as a shortfall rather than a plain fact, which is how *absent* states it.

entries.definition: reveal unintentionally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The teller never meant to tell: it slips out and gives them away, so the fault is the slip, not the intent.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the secrecy in view - what is told was meant to be kept, so the telling counts as a breach.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strips the cover off, suggesting the thing was kept back for a reason, so telling it accuses whoever kept it.
examples: Till I can forget his father, I can never defy or expose him.
Surely there can be no occasion for exposing him so dreadfully.

entries.definition: tell anonymously
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The point is the missing name: the teller stays out of sight, and the word passes no judgement on what is told.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the matter as buried, not just untold, so digging is part of the word - unlike *reveal*.

entries.definition: precisely and clearly expressed or readily observable; leaving nothing to implication
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral base word here: so clear that nothing is left to work out, without praising or criticising that clarity.

entries.definition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral, covering both a meaning never spelled out and one that sits in a thing's nature, where *unspoken* covers only the first.
examples: an implicit agreement not to raise the subject
there was implicit criticism in his voice
anger was implicit in the argument
the oak is implicit in the acorn

entries.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A linking phrase, not a quality: it must name what the meaning lies in, which *inherent* and *underlying* need not.

entries.definition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Built as 'not explicit', it sees the telling as falling short, where *implicit* sees a quality of the thing itself.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Sounds clinical: the gap is a failure to put something into words, not a silence with any weight to it.

entries.definition: exhibiting or calling for sportsmanship or fair play
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises by what is missing - nothing foul in the play - where *sportsmanlike* names the good quality directly.

entries.definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval no one can argue with: it confirms nobody was favored or tricked, without the weight of principle *just* carries.

entries.definition: beyond or deviating from the usual or expected
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flatly notes that something strays from the usual or expected, with none of *peculiar*'s second look.

entries.definition: expressing or manifesting praise or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal to the point of stiffness - the same praise as *approving*, raised into official language.

entries.definition: being favorably inclined
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest here: a leaning in someone's favour, not praise, so nothing has to be shown as it does with *approving*.

entries.definition: not appropriate in application; defective
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and softened: it calls a thing unsuited to its use and faulty, while sounding sorry about it, where *inept* simply condemns.
examples: the infelicitous typesetting was due to illegible copy

entries.definition: not brought to the desired final state
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faintly disapproving: it measures the thing against the final state that was wanted, so it records falling short, not just a stage.

entries.definition: natural and unstudied
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving, and sounds like easy talk: it praises being natural rather than put on, where *informal* only notes what is missing.

entries.definition: without ceremony or formality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pictures the ceremony or formality as stripped off, with an abrupt, blunt edge that *casual* never carries.

entries.definition: in a more fortunate or prosperous condition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Built as a comparison - it always means better than something, and never says what.
examples: she would have been better off if she had stuck with teaching
is better off than his classmate

entries.definition: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Deeply thankful - the timing was so right it tempts you to say heaven stepped in.
examples: a heaven-sent rain saved the crops

entries.definition: most unfortunate or miserable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Holds nothing back - misfortune or misery as bad as it gets, where *unfortunate* only notes that luck ran out.
examples: the most abject slaves joined in the revolt

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the ruin feel bound to happen, as though the outcome were fixed before the event - a heavy seriousness *disastrous* never claims.

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word, for someone without a roof or without inner security, with none of the sense of being wronged in *dispossessed*.

entries.definition: smelling like cedar
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Takes its smell from a wood and names the whole tree, where *balsam-scented* narrows to a resin.

entries.definition: smelling of cinnamon
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Warm where *mint-scented* is cool, but the warmth belongs to the spice, not the word, which names the smell flatly.

entries.definition: having odor or a characteristic odor
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The base word: having a smell, or a smell of its own, and the only one here that never says which smell.

entries.definition: having lost freshness through passage of time
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Understated, almost a gentler way to say *stale*: it notes only that time has passed and taken the freshness with it.
examples: dogs attempting to catch a cold scent

entries.definition: dried out
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names lost moisture, not foulness: a fault of texture, with none of the disgust in *rotten* or *rancid*.
examples: hard dry rolls left over from the day before

entries.definition: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same eggs and larvae as *flyblown*, but with the crawling maggots right in front of you - the harder word to hear.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of the three words for mold seen on the food or smelled off it, with none of *moldy*'s bluntness.

entries.definition: (used of decomposing oils or fats) having a rank smell or taste usually due to a chemical change or decomposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the strong, foul smell or taste of decaying fats and oils - an accusation from the senses, not *bad*'s bare ruling.

entries.definition: lacking freshness, palatability, or showing deterioration from age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word for lost freshness - taste gone, or condition gone with age - where *bad* goes further: unfit to eat.

entries.definition: the act of hindering or obstructing or impeding
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The broadest of the three, covering holding back, blocking and slowing alike, and picturing the act as a course disrupted from outside.
examples: She looked at her father to entreat his interference, lest Mary should be singing all night.
never had she before been so much disposed to pardon his interference in the views of his friend

entries.definition: not functioning properly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest word here — it notes that something is off without saying how far or how badly.

entries.definition: giving or spending with reluctance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A softer word: *close with money* is what you say when you do not want to say *stingy*.
examples: very close (or near) with his money

entries.definition: giving or spending with reluctance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A gentler word for stinginess, softening it into just being *close* with money.
examples: very close (or near) with his money

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Milder than *divine* and *elysian*: it credits the excellence to something breathed in from outside, but names no gods.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hints rather than accuses: the evil lies behind what is seen, in a thing's source as much as in the thing itself.
examples: Darth Vader of the dark side

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and bookish where *atrocious* is loud: the same charge of brutality, made coldly.

entries.definition: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Very old-fashioned and fancy - bad temper dressed up as a physical illness, and hard to say with a straight face.

entries.definition: occurring unexpectedly and requiring urgent action
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and practical beside *explosive*: the unexpected counts only because it demands urgent action, not because it startles.

entries.definition: characterized by physical or psychological maltreatment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here, since the harm is a person treated cruelly in body or mind, not the general damage *harmful* allows.
examples: argued … that foster homes are abusive

entries.definition: causing mental or emotional injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrows the body's word for hurt to mind or feelings: the damage is a blow that leaves a mark, not *harmful*'s bare capacity.
examples: protected from the bruising facts of battle

entries.definition: harmful to living things
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and clinical, it records damage to living things as a finding, not a complaint, cooling what *hurtful* says plainly.

entries.definition: (used of statements) harmful and often untrue; tending to discredit or malign
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and it marks the statement as the kind that makes someone look small, where *denigrating* catches the act as it happens.

entries.definition: harmful to living things
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain-spoken one of its three, naming the same damage to living things in everyday language that *deleterious* and *injurious* refuse.

entries.definition: not affected by jaundice
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A medical word that says only that jaundice is absent, with none of the approval the other words here carry.

entries.definition: not easily borne; wearing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The difficulty sits in the thing: a load fixed on you that must be carried, not merely a strain that tires.
examples: the burdensome task of preparing the income tax return

entries.definition: causing distress or worry or anxiety
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: It stirs a settled mind out of its calm - a lighter, briefer trouble than the unease *disturbing* keeps up.
examples: a revelation that was most perturbing

entries.definition: worthy of the greatest honor or distinction
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Goes past granting honor to set its subject at the very top of it, where *honorable* only confirms the honor is deserved.
examples: The nation's pediatrician laureate is preparing to lay down his black bag

entries.definition: arising from or marked by despair or loss of hope
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points at the despair itself, whether a thing comes from lost hope or just shows it, where *hopeless* points at the chances.
examples: a despairing view of the world situation
the last despairing plea of the condemned criminal

entries.definition: unable to function; without help
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Two failures at once, unable to function and no help at hand, so it sounds like a plea, not *hopeless*'s verdict.

entries.definition: without hope because there seems to be no possibility of comfort or success
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain verdict: no hope because no comfort or success looks possible - about the odds, where *despairing* is about the feeling.
examples: in an agony of hopeless grief
with a hopeless sigh he sat down

entries.definition: without hope of solution
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Aimed at the problem, not at anyone: a flat statement that no solution can be hoped for, with no blame in it.

entries.definition: unable to function; without help
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Unable to function and without help, like *helpless*, but as a settled state rather than a moment, so it sounds beyond rescue.

entries.definition: showing utter resignation or hopelessness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Simply “not hopeful”: the same utter resignation or hopelessness as *abject*, but without the scorn, saying less than it means.

entries.definition: extended meanings; especially of psychological coldness; without human warmth or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word: it names missing human warmth without deciding whether that is a settled nature or a snub aimed at someone.

entries.definition: so surprisingly impressive as to stun or overwhelm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A heavier landing than *astonishing* - the surprise is not just noticed, it takes the ground out from under you.

entries.definition: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal - it describes what a thing does to the people who see it, where *amazing* simply cries out.
examples: the Grand Canyon is an awe-inspiring sight

entries.definition: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A flat word that states the effect and stops, with none of the speaker's own delight that *awesome* shows openly.
examples: Westminster Hall's awing majesty, so vast, so high, so silent

entries.definition: easily seen or detected
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Almost technical in feel: something a look or a test turns up, where *perceptible* is something the senses take in.

entries.definition: strongly marked; easily noticeable
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Raises the degree, not the ease: the thing stands out by how strongly it shows, not by how easily it is found.

entries.definition: capable or worthy of being noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word: able to be noticed or worth noticing, without saying whether that is welcome, which is what *obtrusive* adds.
examples: noticeable for its vivid historical background

entries.definition: undesirably noticeable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one word here that judges: as noticeable as it gets, and unwanted, where *marked* only measures how much.
examples: the obtrusive behavior of a spoiled child

entries.definition: having more than the average number of accidents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly blaming - it turns a count of accidents into a fixed quality, so they seem caused by whatever it describes, not by chance.

entries.definition: designed to promote discipline
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Official, and a gentler way to name discipline - it is what discipline is called in a report.
examples: the teacher's action was corrective rather than instructional

entries.definition: designed to promote discipline
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names correction or punishment in neutral, official language.
examples: the mother was stern and disciplinary

entries.definition: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The softest word here for real physical injury: it carries its lean toward battle lightly and shows nothing of the wound.
examples: ambulances … for the hurt men and women

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The ordinary *-ed* form for that same ragged tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays curt.

entries.definition: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same bruising, but heavy and grim, as if something has gone badly wrong under the skin, where *black-and-blue* stays almost homely.

entries.definition: having the surface exposed and painful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports pain where the jagged-edge words report shape: the covering is gone, leaving what lies under it exposed and stinging.

entries.definition: deserving blame
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest blame word: it says where blame lies but not what kind of act it was, while *guilty* calls the act wrong.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Like *blamable*, it shows no personal feeling, treating the wrong, the evil and the merely harmful alike, in one steady tone.

entries.definition: guilty of murder or bloodshed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most serious here: guilt for killing, which the word treats as a stain carried rather than a charge answered.

entries.definition: guilty of a misdeed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Lighter than *criminal* because the deed is smaller: it scolds a wrong rather than condemning a crime.

entries.definition: liable to a fine
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: As dry as *finable*: a penalty applies, and nothing is said about the wrong or the person who did it.

entries.definition: responsible for or chargeable with a reprehensible act
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain verdict, covering both the one who did the wrong and the one who could merely be charged with it.

entries.definition: highly cultured or educated
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same claim to being highly cultured as *highbrow*, but the *-ed* ending makes it sit heavier and stiffer.

entries.definition: sufficiently interesting to be reported in a newspaper
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bar to clear, not a compliment: it asks whether something has enough interest to report, where *interesting* describes the pull itself.

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: It stresses slowness: ground taken bit by bit, so no single step looks like the violation *invasive* makes it sound.
examples: we moved back from the encroaching tide

entries.definition: tending to intrude (especially upon privacy)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for the fault: it names the pushing-in itself, without the scorn in *meddlesome*.
examples: she felt her presence there was intrusive

entries.definition: tending to impart new life and vigor to
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval for a lift that brings back lost life and energy, rather than giving them for the first time like *life-giving*.
examples: the renewing warmth of the sunshine

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, calm approval: it steadies you and gives you energy, but does not delight you like the louder *exhilarating*.

entries.definition: acceptable to your conscience
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A low, inner bar: the thing satisfies your conscience rather than being right in itself - far weaker approval than *fitting*.

entries.definition: being precisely fitting and right
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same verdict as *fitting*, declared in a serious, formal way, so the rightness sounds handed down rather than noticed.
examples: it is only meet that she should be seated first

entries.definition: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool and measured: it approves the match between what is deserved and what is dealt out, not what is dealt out itself.

entries.definition: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same verdict as *retributive*, but more mechanical - it sounds like the machinery of paying back, not the principle behind it.

entries.definition: most familiar or renowned
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Ranks one above all the rest for being known, but claims nothing grander than that first place.
examples: Stevenson's best-known work is probably ‘Treasure Island’

entries.definition: more familiar or renowned than the other of two
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Narrow - it compares exactly two and gives one the edge, not the top spot among all as *best-known* does.
examples: the better-known book of the two

entries.definition: lost temporarily; as especially put in an unaccustomed or forgotten place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same temporary loss as *mislaid*, but the fault lies in where it ended up, not in setting it down.

entries.definition: (of an animal) having no home or having wandered away from home
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pity and a touch of nuisance at once, for an animal with no home or one that has wandered off.

entries.definition: unable to find your way
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Only the passing trouble of not finding your way, with no blame in it - unlike the lasting state *stray* describes.

entries.definition: not used to good advantage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says that value came to nothing without pointing at anyone to blame, which is what *squandered* adds.

entries.definition: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise at full strength, where *lovable* only describes: you cannot help loving it for being naive or like a child.

entries.definition: inviting cuddling or hugging
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Soft, casual and physical: it charms by asking to be cuddled or hugged, not by a good nature as in *sweet*.

entries.definition: devoid of significance or force
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Takes the air out of a thing, saying only that nothing of weight is there, and leaves the insult to *vacuous*.

entries.definition: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Openly scornful, not just total - it sneers at the very thing it strengthens, where *complete* only measures it.

entries.definition: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the quality total as if it were a finished achievement, and that mismatch gives it a dry humour *utter* lacks.

entries.definition: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds a fed-up annoyance, insisting the quality never lets up, where *utter* simply states how far it goes.

entries.definition: without qualification; used informally as (often pejorative) intensifiers
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most deliberate of these, spelling out that nothing was mixed in to weaken the quality, where *pure* says it in a breath.

entries.definition: far beyond a norm in quantity or amount or degree; to an utmost degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the utmost degree flatly, measuring how far an amount or degree sits from the norm without calling that a fault.

entries.definition: beyond a norm in opinion or actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Just a position: it puts an opinion or action past the norm and leaves the judging to others, where *outrageous* is all judgement.

entries.definition: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dry: a big excess becomes a grumble, where *outrageous* turns the same excess into a protest.

entries.definition: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not just distance but too much: an opinion or action pushed past what its own position would allow, where *far* stays neutral.

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the excess for not being justified rather than for its size - the quietest complaint of the words meaning beyond normal limits.
examples: his dress stops just short of undue elegance

entries.definition: arousing affect
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest of the three — it says feeling was caused and stops there, where *poignant* and *touching* each put force behind it.
examples: the homecoming of the released hostages was an affecting scene

entries.definition: having particular physiological functions augmented or replaced by electronic or electromechanical components
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Strictly technical — body functions boosted or replaced by machines, without the sense of lack the other words here attach to made things.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The easiest word here to hear without complaint: anything beyond what is needed can simply be available, where *superfluous* would call it waste.
examples: found some extra change lying on the dresser
extra ribs as well as other supernumerary internal parts

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: An accounting word: it records the amount left over as a balance, with no complaint about it.
examples: surplus cheese distributed to the needy

entries.definition: very unpleasant or offensive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British slang - the unpleasantness is felt as dislike of something shabby and dirty, not the moral judgement in *filthy*.

entries.definition: having or showing or indicative of high or elevated character
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The basic word here for the thing itself: having high character, showing it, or merely pointing to it.

entries.definition: not noticed inadvertently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same accidental slip as *disregarded*, but implying the thing once held attention and lost it, leaving it a little less important.
examples: her aching muscles forgotten she danced all night
he was scolded for his forgotten chores

entries.definition: disregarded
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the three: something was there to attend to, without *ignored*'s choice or *neglected*'s failure of care.

entries.definition: not noticed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat, basic word: it says only that the thing was not noticed, blaming no one and giving it no claim on attention.
examples: hoped his departure had passed unnoticed

entries.definition: not perceived or commented on
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and abstract, covering both not noticing a thing and saying nothing of it, with the weight on the noticing.

entries.definition: not perceived or commented on
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Leans the other way from *unperceived*: the thing may well have been seen, and the point is that nothing was said of it.

entries.definition: easily perceived and understood
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The basic, neutral word of the group: the thing takes no effort to see or understand, without *axiomatic*'s claim about proof.

entries.definition: needing no explanation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The thing explains itself, so nothing needs to be added - where *obvious* only says it is easy to grasp.

entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, it presents advanced years as a settled state, where *older* only marks a point on a scale.

entries.definition: of or like a feeble old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal-sounding but withering, covering both being a feeble old woman and merely being like one; the scorn is in the word itself.

entries.definition: (of fabrics and paper) grown dark in color over time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The only word here about what time does to the colour of cloth or paper, not to a life, and it judges nothing.
examples: the darkened margins of the paper

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful where *aged* is not: weakness of mind or body from age becomes the whole of what it says about the person.
examples: his mother was doddering and frail

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same judgement of weakness from age as *doddering*, but the shorter form makes the mockery sound casual rather than deliberate.

entries.definition: mentally or physically infirm with age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and blunt - the same weakness from age as *doddering*, in a word too jokey to leave the person any dignity.

entries.definition: (used especially of persons) having lived for a relatively long time or attained a specific age
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and neutral, it covers both a long life lived and simply a stated age reached, where *of age* means only the second.

entries.definition: advanced in years; (‘aged’ is pronounced as two syllables)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: An *-er* form used as plain description, which makes it the softest word here: it suggests a scale rather than naming a state.

entries.definition: growing old
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical and detached: the same growing old as *aging*, in a style that feels nothing about it.

entries.definition: (of children and animals) young, immature
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmth is in the smallness: calling a child or young animal little makes it lovable, where *small* only measures.
examples: what a big little boy you are
Her little brother was not yet old enough for school.

entries.definition: young and immature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Youth felt as softness: being not fully grown is something easily broken, not something admired.

entries.definition: expecting a rise in prices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A stance, not a judgement: it names an expectation of rising prices, and unlike *optimistic* says nothing about the person holding it.

entries.definition: reflecting optimism
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the optimism in what is shown, not in whoever holds it - it colours a view instead of judging a person's nature.
examples: looked at the world through rose-colored glasses

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disarray or confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the lost order as a state the thing has been put into and left in, without the damage *broken* implies.

entries.definition: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarse and total - a tangle or dead stop treated as a mess someone made and must answer for; the harshest word here.

entries.definition: snarled or stalled in complete confusion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same total tangle or standstill under a short, almost casual label - a sad smile where *fucked-up* is furious.

entries.definition: not efficient or methodical
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The calmest criticism here: it blames missing method and the wasted effort that follows, picturing no wreckage at all.
examples: the project failed through unmethodical planning

entries.definition: thrown into a state of disorganization or incoherence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures the collapse as a coming-apart: what was holding gives way, and the thing falls into disorder or stops making sense.
examples: price programs became unstuck because little grain was available

entries.definition: radically new or original
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval for newness pushed to its edge, where breaking with what came before is everything - a bigger claim than *fresh* makes.

entries.definition: done by hand without mechanical aids or devices
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely about method - the hand working without mechanical aid or device - with none of the approval the words beside it carry.

entries.definition: not derivative or imitative
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a thing by what it is not - not taken from a source, not a copy - and, unlike *original*, claims no freshness.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault in being ordinary, not damaged: the thing is found everywhere, where *threadbare* sees it worn thin.
examples: his remarks were trite and commonplace

entries.definition: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier and fuller-sounding than *platitudinal*, and the word's own size is part of the mockery: dullness dressed up, then shown up.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the wear down to time, not to any user - unlike *hackneyed*, which blames someone for running the thing into the ground.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the thing for mileage, not damage: used so often nothing in it can still surprise, milder than the ruin *threadbare* finds.

entries.definition: with no effort to conceal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusing where *bald* is only blunt: not trying to hide it shows nerve, something they should have been ashamed to show.

entries.definition: plain to see
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Mentions disguise only to deny it, suggesting that what is plain to see could have been hidden and was not.

entries.definition: causing physical or psychological pain
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word: it says something hurts, in the body or the mind, without saying how sharply or how much.

entries.definition: showing patient and unruffled self-control and restraint under adversity; slow to retaliate or express resentment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Patience when provoked, in the most formal word for it.
examples: was longanimous in the face of suffering

entries.definition: fanatically patriotic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The sharpest word in the group, hearing the extreme patriotism as eagerness to fight rather than just too much enthusiasm.

entries.definition: inspired by love for your country
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same love of country, but as faithful attachment rather than passion - quieter and less openly shown than *patriotic*.

entries.definition: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Goes beyond flaws and marks to anything mixed in that spoils it, so it can describe a substance, not only a performance.
examples: the clear complexion of a healthy young woman

entries.definition: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal where *complete* is plain, and it turns having every needed quality into the highest kind of praise.

entries.definition: without fault or error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Treats being without fault as something kept whole rather than achieved, and sounds stiffer than *faultless*.

entries.definition: without a flaw
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Simply says there is no flaw, without the admiration that *flawless* carries.

entries.definition: containing errors or alterations
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Errors or changes have got in, so it can't be trusted as it is - heavier than *flawed*, where the whole stays sound.

entries.definition: containing errors or alterations
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points back to a sound original that errors or changes have since got into, where *corrupt* just describes how it is now.
examples: spoke a corrupted version of the language

entries.definition: having a defect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ordinary and fixable - it finds a fault to be put right rather than writing the thing off the way *defective* does.

entries.definition: not perfect; defective or inadequate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for falling short of perfect - it stops there, without *defective*'s suggestion that something inside has gone wrong.
examples: had only an imperfect understanding of his responsibilities

entries.definition: not created for a particular occasion
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Describes without judging: it marks a thing as kept ready for whatever comes, instead of set up for one occasion.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at the mind as the thing being used, in a higher style than *mental*, passing no judgment on the work done.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most abstract and academic of the set, naming mind-work in a high style where *mental* stays flat.

entries.definition: affecting or influenced by the human mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Works both ways, covering what the mind affects and what affects it, where *psychogenic* looks only at where a thing began.

entries.definition: of or associated with or requiring the use of the mind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at the mind as what is doing the work, not at whether its results are sound: a label, not a judgment.
examples: the triumph of the rational over the animal side of man

entries.definition: fail to meet the hopes or expectations of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply fall short, without *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.
examples: Here are officers enough at Meryton to disappoint all the young ladies in the country.
Miss Bingley, however, was incapable of disappointing Mr. Darcy in anything

entries.definition: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not being there when relied on, whether by proving unreliable or by walking away, but framed as a lapse rather than a wrong.
examples: Elizabeth's courage did not fail her.

entries.definition: greatly annoyed; out of patience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British, and it takes the drama out: patience fully lost, in a phrase too casual to shout, where *exasperated* keeps its calm.

entries.definition: having a strong distaste from surfeit
