entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strong dislike from having had too much of something - the stomach turning, not anger aimed at anyone.

entries.definition: not pleased; experiencing or manifesting displeasure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The coolest word here: it names a lack of pleasure, felt or shown, without any heat in it.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Light: it treats the feeling as a small thing and the person as easily upset, where *annoyed* judges neither.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rude and blunt: the crudest way in this group to say it, and everything *displeased* holds back.
examples: felt really pissed at her snootiness

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Churning, not flaring: the feeling is muddy and unsettled all through, where *stung* is one sharp point.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Something landed, and the feeling is the sudden pull back from it, where *irritated* only wears on.

entries.definition: inspiring admiration or approval
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval with respect in it - you look up to the thing rather than just enjoy it, a more serious word than *charming*.
examples: among her many admirable qualities are generosity and graciousness

entries.definition: capable of winning favor
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures pleasing by the favour won, not the pleasure given, so it leans away from praising the thing at all, unlike *charming*.
examples: with open arms and an ingratiating smile

entries.definition: capable of being attained or accomplished
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and homely, it makes the thing sound simply within arm's length, where *attainable* makes the reach sound impressive.
examples: art is not something that is come-at-able by dint of study

entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most procedural of the set: it asks only whether the steps can be carried out, not whether they should be.

entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A practical judgement, not a hope: the thing can be done with what is at hand now, a test *possible* never applies.

entries.definition: capable of happening or existing
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare minimum: it says only that the thing is not ruled out, promising nothing about anyone managing to do it.
examples: a breakthrough may be possible next year

entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest backing here: it calls a plan solid enough to go ahead as things stand, where *workable* says only it will work.

entries.definition: foolish; totally unsound
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Joking - the foolishness is treated as amusing oddness, so it stings less than *crazy*, though the verdict is the same.
examples: a screwball proposal without a prayer of working

entries.definition: unerringly accurate
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and total: accuracy with no room for error at all, where *precise* can still be more or less exact.

entries.definition: precisely as stated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain emphasis, insisting the thing is exactly the one stated and carrying no praise or blame with it.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same promise as *arable*, seen through the act of cultivating: an open possibility, not a fixed label for the land.

entries.definition: yielding material gain or profit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat starting point: it reports a gain but not its size or how welcome it is - the two things *juicy* adds.
examples: profitable speculation on the stock market

entries.definition: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest and widest here, praising a mind that cuts through or a feeling that runs deep, where *deep* stays with thinking.

entries.definition: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A label, not praise: something is proper or legitimate under Muslim law, and the approval is the law's, not the speaker's.
examples: the fund earns halal profits in full compliance with the Shari'a

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful: being too proper is taken as smugness, correct behaviour shown off as a mark of being better than others.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest fault here: a sense of what is proper held so tightly it goes stiff, mocked rather than condemned.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Too proper to the point of being easily shocked, and so a harsher word than *prim*.

entries.definition: not suitable or right or appropriate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest disapproval here - it marks a thing as not fitting without naming the standard it fails, where *unseemly* and *indecent* name one.
examples: slightly improper to dine alone with a married man
improper attire for the golf course

entries.definition: improper or even offensive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds mild but runs from merely improper to offensive, and saying it so mildly gives the offensive end its force.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faint and formal - it treats falling short of accepted standards as unattractive rather than shocking, staying well back from *indecent*.

entries.definition: humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves of a quiet, held-back manner - mildness as a virtue, though the meaning can come close to giving in to others.

entries.definition: causing or tending to cause anger or resentment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-ing* form keeps the effect happening: anger or resentment being stirred now, where *agitative* names a settled quality.

entries.definition: capable of producing violent emotion or arousing controversy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A load waiting to go off: violent feeling or controversy stored up, where *inflammatory* is already at work.
examples: the highly charged issue of abortion

entries.definition: arousing to action or rebellion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heat is the whole point: the thing is what lights the fire of action or rebellion, not just the occasion for it.

entries.definition: serving or tending to provoke, excite, or stimulate; stimulating discussion or exciting controversy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral: the power to excite, stir or set off controversy, without saying if that is welcome, where *provoking* narrows it to anger.
examples: provocative Irish tunes which … compel the hearers to dance

entries.definition: rousing to activity or heightened action as by spurring or goading
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one welcome stirring here, though the push behind it keeps an edge of being driven to act rather than persuaded.
examples: tossed a rousing political comment into the conversation

entries.definition: (of sound or color) free from anything that dulls or dims
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a sound or colour that nothing dulls or dims - brightness is the point, not the lack of dirt that *clean* marks.

entries.definition: as found in nature in the elemental form
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Simply describes: the thing is found in nature already in its elemental form, and no credit is given for that.

entries.definition: not mixed with extraneous elements
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest word here: it says nothing that does not belong is mixed in, and neither praises nor criticizes that.

entries.definition: free of extraneous elements of any kind
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The broadest word here: nothing that does not belong, of any kind, survives it, where *clean* only rules out dirt.
examples: the violin's pure and lovely song

entries.definition: (of an alcoholic drink) stirred or shaken with ice, but served without it
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A serving instruction, not a judgement: the drink was stirred or shaken with ice, then served without it.
examples: I like my martinis straight up

entries.definition: (of sound or color) free from anything that dulls or dims
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: With its *un-*, it praises a sound or colour by naming what fails to cloud it, where *clear* simply states the brightness.

entries.definition: free of restrictions or qualifications
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same freedom as *clean*, but as an open way through: nothing in the way, rather than nothing left over.

entries.definition: not modified or restricted by reservations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A blunt single syllable that shuts the door on reservations, where *categorical* refuses them like a formal declaration.

entries.definition: endowed with the capacity to reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns the simple ability to reason into a compliment, where *reasoning* and *thinking* only note that the ability is there.

entries.definition: marked by sound judgment; having good reason
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sound judgment as the basic standard a mind must meet, not a prize it wins, which gives it a weight *reasonable* lacks.

entries.definition: exhibiting native good judgment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heaviest of the *commonsense* forms: its extra ending makes the same praise sound clumsier than crisp *commonsense* itself.

entries.definition: based on sound reasoning or evidence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The coolest, most reluctant approval here: the reasoning can be defended, where *well-founded* says its grounds are solid.

entries.definition: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and settled, covering belief as well as purpose: firmness as a lasting quality of the person, not a stand taken once.

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Not to be shaken, but because it does not bend - the resolve seems unbending as much as strong.

entries.definition: cheerfully irresponsible
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Showy boldness rather than lightness - it shows off not caring, where *carefree* simply has no worry to shed.

entries.definition: cheerfully irresponsible
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Its sing-song rhyme makes the cheer sound silly and disorganized, tipping into criticism where *happy-go-lucky* stays fond.

entries.definition: free from control or responsibility
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Simply states where someone stands - there is no one to answer to, and the person is not judged for it.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight of a legal charge behind blame that is moral, not legal - an outcry where *condemnable* is a ruling.

entries.definition: moving at very high speed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The danger is in the picture, not a verdict: a pace fast enough to break a neck, which can sound thrilling or reckless.

entries.definition: (of persons) dangerously reckless or violent as from urgency or despair
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Said of a person, not a situation: past caution and likely to turn violent; the despair behind it does not soften the warning.

entries.definition: involving risk or danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and classifying - it records danger as a feature to be measured, cooler than *risky*, which sounds like advice.

entries.definition: strikingly different; tending to contrast
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same striking difference as *contrasting*, but framed as a quality a thing has rather than an effect it produces.

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the difference a matter of telling things apart, so it holds up to a close look, where *distinct* just states it.

entries.definition: diverging from another or from a standard
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes difference a moving apart - from another thing or from a standard - where *disparate* simply finds two things unlike.

entries.definition: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The attraction works like a spell that holds you, so the hope it raises feels made by magic, where *alluring* simply glows.
examples: the voice was low and beguiling

entries.definition: beguiling but harmful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The warning is in the pairing: the charm is real and is exactly what hides the harm, where *corrupting* names the damage openly.

entries.definition: tending to entice into a desired action or state
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain name for the pull toward something wanted: it measures how strong the pull is, not where it leads, unlike *corrupting*.

entries.definition: highly attractive and able to arouse hope or desire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The desire it raises may be one you argue with yourself over, so the pull feels like pressure, not *enticing*'s clean invitation.

entries.definition: absorbed in your own interests or thoughts etc
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same fault as *self-absorbed*, easy to forgive, and the milder way to say it.

entries.definition: having a higher rank
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Means just what it says - higher in rank than another - and implies nothing past the position itself.

entries.definition: having precedence (especially because of longer service)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and procedural: it turns seniority into a right to go first, a right *senior* leaves unsaid.
examples: precedential treatment for senior members of the firm

entries.definition: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mockery that goes past unserious to empty: nothing inside to be serious with, where *dizzy* only sets the head spinning.

entries.definition: showing inappropriate levity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The verdict is built in, since the lightness is out of place: it scolds a manner, where *empty-headed* diagnoses a mind.

entries.definition: not serious in content or attitude or behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word here and the widest, fitting content, attitude or behaviour alike, without the hollow-head picture of *airheaded* or *empty-headed*.

entries.definition: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same fault as *giddy*, stated as a quality of the head rather than a mood.

entries.definition: lacking seriousness; given to frivolity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest, most forgiving word: it names the fault without picturing the head, and leaves room for fondness that *airheaded* shuts out.

entries.definition: important in effect or meaning
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More insistent than *significant*: it claims the thing matters and should be treated that way, not only that it counts.

entries.definition: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The highest praise - skill carried to its finish with nothing left to add, far above the everyday *proficient*.

entries.definition: having or showing or requiring special skill
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, checkable praise that credits skill without admiring it, and can describe work that needs skill as well as people who have it.
examples: only the most skilled gymnasts make an Olympic team
a skilled surgeon has many years of training and experience
a skilled reconstruction of her damaged elbow

entries.definition: showing lack of art
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names something missing, not a mess - the work shows no art, a lighter complaint than the spoiling *botched* points at.

entries.definition: poorly done
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive, with a touch of scorn - the badness is rough and uneven, plain to see in the thing itself.

entries.definition: showing lack of skill or aptitude
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the lack of skill or ability a lasting quality - not one attempt gone wrong but the person's way of doing things.

entries.definition: of a person unable to do something skillfully
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at the person, not the result - it writes off their ability, with a fed-up feeling that can slide into fondness.

entries.definition: not having or showing or requiring special skill or proficiency
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Labels rather than condemns - it fits work needing no special skill as evenly as a worker without it, where *botchy* judges the result.
examples: unskilled in the art of rhetoric
workers in unskilled occupations are finding fewer and fewer job opportunities

entries.definition: poorly done
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat word here: it says only that the work fell short of skill, with none of the disgust in *butcherly*.

entries.definition: very sophisticated especially because of surfeit; versed in the ways of the world
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sophistication from having had too much, which sours the praise: the person is past being impressed, where *worldly* only means experienced.
examples: the blase traveler refers to the ocean he has crossed as ‘the pond’

entries.definition: having or appealing to those having worldly knowledge and refinement and savoir-faire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises worldly knowledge and refinement together, and can describe things made for such people, not just the people - which *urbane* cannot.

entries.definition: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for buying, turned on a person, hints scornfully that they had a price, where *bribe* names the crime.
examples: They said the inspector had been bought and would report whatever he was told.

entries.definition: lacking energy or vitality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical in tone, presenting a lack of energy as a condition to be observed rather than a failing to be judged.

entries.definition: lacking energy or vitality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical, not judging: the lack of energy sounds like a lasting feature, not the passing drain that *enervated* suggests.

entries.definition: lacking strength or vigor
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsher than *faint*: the lack invites pity, and the pity slides into a judgement that it could never be enough.

entries.definition: wanting in physical strength
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, basic word here: it names missing physical strength and stops, where sharper words add an attitude to it.

entries.definition: very lively and profitable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The *-ing* form keeps the gain in motion - still climbing, where *prosperous* names a state already reached.

entries.definition: doomed to extinction
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grave rather than informal: the ending is total and stated with no pleasure in it, where *washed-up* shows scorn.

entries.definition: of or characteristic of low rank or importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts a thing below others and lets that ranking carry the sting, where *humble* names the same low place without ranking it.

entries.definition: decisively surpassed by something else so as to appear to be of a lower class
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The strongest here: the low standing comes from a contest clearly lost, and carries the humiliation of the comparison.

entries.definition: low or inferior in station or quality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shrinks rather than ranks: the low quality comes across as being unimportant, not as a place on a ladder.

entries.definition: of low or inferior quality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A cold comparison - it needs something better to exist before it means anything.

entries.definition: made of inferior workmanship and materials
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cheapness trying to look flashy - which is what makes it worth scorn, not merely poor.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Holds the same menace as *feral*, but in stiffer, more formal language.

entries.definition: not subdued or trained for service or use
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neither brought under control nor trained for service or use - its wildness is measured by what it has not been made to do.

entries.definition: not domesticated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Just 'not domesticated' and nothing more - the plainest word here, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

entries.definition: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same natural state as *wild*, but described by what was never done to it: a taming that never happened.

entries.definition: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blames the state for confusing anyone following it: no order, nothing predictable, where *wild* only says control is gone.

entries.definition: marked by extreme lack of restraint or control
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names how extreme the missing restraint is without colouring it, and leans negative only because that lack is extreme rather than partial.

entries.definition: characterized by thriftiness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flat word: it names care with resources as a lasting trait, without pressing the approval *thrifty* carries.
examples: wealthy by inheritance but saving by constitution

entries.definition: not able to be supported or defended
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Moves the fault from what cannot be borne to what cannot be defended: the weakness is the thing's own, not anyone's strain.

entries.definition: (of persons) worthy of trust or confidence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The *-ed* form makes the trust something others give, where *sure* names a quality the person carries on their own.

entries.definition: murder without leaving a trace on the body
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Chilling because so exact: it names the killing by its method, no trace left on the body, where *murder* is general.

entries.definition: kill intentionally and with premeditation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most indirect way here to say it: a planned killing made to sound like tidying, its intent hidden behind a bland word.

entries.definition: (of persons) taken advantage of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and seen from the sufferer's side: the person visibly feels the wrong, where *ill-used* and *exploited* only report it.

entries.definition: (of persons) taken advantage of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bare and cutting: the word alone reduces the person to a tool, saying far less than *exploited* and landing colder for it.
examples: after going out of his way to help his friend get the job he felt not appreciated but used

entries.definition: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and heavy in sound: the same extreme, deeply criminal verdict as *heinous*, in grander words.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the same refusal - it cannot be reformed - but its blunt *un-* start sounds more everyday than *irredeemable*.

entries.definition: susceptible to attack
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat, basic word here: it notes that an attack could land, without saying anything is missing or anyone is at fault.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the laugh the thing draws, dismissing it with amusement where *preposterous* rejects it out loud.
examples: a contribution so small as to be laughable

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and angry, rejecting the absurdity out loud rather than just laughing at it as *laughable* does.
examples: a preposterous attempt to turn back the pages of history

entries.definition: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful and vivid - it adds filth to simple wear and tear.

entries.definition: (often used ironically) worthy of being treated in a particular way
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral on its face: it says some treatment is fitting, never that the treatment is good, which lets it turn ironic.

entries.definition: harshness of manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for the same harshness, felt as a cutting edge in how someone treats you, not *asperity*'s formal verdict on them.

entries.definition: a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not a passing mood but a settled tendency to anger that gets out of hand - an accusation about someone's character.
examples: his temper was well known to all his employees
He has a temper, and everyone at work knows to keep out of his way.

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stresses not caring over staying calm, so the calm looks like something missing, and carries a faint blame that *unconcern* avoids.
examples: He listened to her with perfect indifference
With an air of indifference, he soon afterwards added

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Stresses the calm, casual side - an untroubled evenness that may only be on the surface, without *indifference*'s hint that nothing is felt.

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of the same misleading surface: a respectable tint lent to something so it passes, only a tint, where *disguise* covers.
examples: His story was only a colour to hide what he had really done.

entries.definition: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Like *pretence*, a cunning or faked appearance, but pictured as something put on and worn, so the deceit lies in taking it on.
examples: under the guise of friendship he betrayed them

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The barest word here, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the deceit unsaid, where *pretence* puts the trick on show.
examples: he hoped his claims would have a semblance of authenticity

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest word here: it records that damage happened and judges nothing, where *scar* insists the damage lasted.

entries.definition: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise in this sense, a kind quality, but the word tilts down toward the sufferer where *compassion* stands level.

entries.definition: malevolence by virtue of being malicious or spiteful or nasty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ill will that covers plain nastiness as well as a real wish to harm, so it can bite without the threat *malice* carries.
examples: There was a streak of spite in everything she said about her neighbours.

entries.definition: a woman's virtue or chastity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes a woman's chastity her standing, something she is credited with and can be stripped of, where *virtue* only calls it moral.

entries.definition: a lack of caution in practical affairs
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names a fault by what is missing - caution not brought to practical matters - where *rashness* accuses someone of charging ahead.
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia
I see the imprudence of it.

entries.definition: the trait of acting rashly and without prudence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier, since the fault is a trait of the person, not a gap in a decision: acting without caution, not just lacking it.

entries.definition: a disposition free from stress or emotion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Soothing rather than lofty: a nature free of stress, praised as restful, where *serenity* raises it higher.

entries.definition: formal or perfunctory politeness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The lowest here: politeness as outward form, done correctly or gone through without interest, so it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.
examples: his formal civility was just what it had been
hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet's civilities

entries.definition: excellence of manners or social conduct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Not just meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it - the highest of these words, where *civility* is the lowest.

entries.definition: a courteous manner that respects accepted social usage
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest name for behaviour that respects accepted social custom, so mild that the approval barely feels like praise beside *politeness*.

entries.definition: the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or just useful, without *price*'s claim that the quality is great.

entries.definition: knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild approval for the knack of heading off embarrassment or distress, a plain quality where *discretion* sounds like a virtue you are praised for.

entries.definition: the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat name for the ability to tell relations apart, saying only that it is there, without the admiration *sagacity* adds.

entries.definition: something jumbled or confused
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the mess or confusion something you are inside and lost in, complicated in a way *tangle* does not suggest.

entries.definition: a poor example
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Regretful where *excuse* is blunt - the same judgement that it falls short, said with a pained face, not a scornful one.
examples: it was an apology for a meal
The cold soup and dry bread were an apology for a dinner.

entries.definition: an instance that does not conform to a rule or generalization
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names a case by where it stands - outside the rule - and passes no judgement on it for being there.
examples: all her children were brilliant; the only exception was her last child

entries.definition: an impracticable and illusory idea
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The idea is not only unreal but could never be carried out, and the word holds the picture of it bursting.
examples: he didn't want to burst the newcomer's bubble

entries.definition: something many people believe that is false
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest way to call a common belief false: a passing idea, not an accusation against those who hold it.
examples: The notion that lightning never strikes the same place twice is an old fancy.

entries.definition: the ultimate goal for which something is done
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the outcome the final one that everything else serves, and brings the picture of a journey's end that *object* lacks.

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the outcome in the person's own mind, so it holds even if nothing is done, unlike *target*, something that can be hit.
examples: Thus much for my general intention in favour of matrimony

entries.definition: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Dry and formal: the goal as a definite thing to get, one believed within reach, without *target*'s sense of hit or miss.
examples: the sole object of her trip was to see her children
The object of the meeting was to settle the dispute.

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The weightiest plain word for a wanted outcome: it gives the planned action its reason, where *aim* only gives it a direction.
examples: my mother's purpose will be answered
She was going to the butcher's, she told me, on purpose to order in some meat on Wednesday

entries.definition: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The sharpest of these: the reachable outcome becomes a thing to hit, so falling short counts as a miss.

entries.definition: an inclination to favor one group or view or opinion over alternatives
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for leaning toward one side: the scales are tipped, but unlike *prejudice* it does not say the case is closed.
examples: I do not trust my own partiality.
the strong sisterly partiality which made any admiration of Elizabeth appear perfectly natural

entries.definition: a partiality for some particular place
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the leaning by its object, one particular place, so the narrow view is built in, where *partiality* must spell it out.

entries.definition: the justification for some act or belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for justifying an act or belief, saying nothing of whether it succeeds and, unlike *excuse*, assuming no wrong.

entries.definition: a defense of some offensive behavior or some failure to keep a promise etc.
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Admits the fault while covering it - what it defends is already offensive behaviour or a broken promise, where *defence* assumes no wrong.
examples: His pride does not offend me so much as pride often does, because there is an excuse for it.
She was then but fifteen, which must be her excuse.

entries.definition: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bluntly scolding - the disrespectful answer reduced to just talk, named by the body part that made it, not by what it said.

entries.definition: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ruin on the scale of *disaster*, but declared in a grander, more ringing way.
examples: the whole city was affected by the irremediable calamity

entries.definition: an absence of emotion or enthusiasm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, general name: it covers missing emotion and missing enthusiasm alike, and treats the whole absence as a failing.

entries.definition: apathy demonstrated by an absence of emotional reactions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The restrained word: it reports only that no emotional reaction came, where *stolidity* sees the same blankness as dullness in the person.
examples: She heard the news with complete indifference, and her face never changed.

entries.definition: the quality of being worthy of esteem or respect
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Highest and steadiest here: not a feeling about oneself but a worth that earns respect, so never open to *conceit*'s charge of excess.
examples: it was beneath his dignity to cheat
showed his true dignity when under pressure

entries.definition: feelings of excessive pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cuts the pride down to size: the same excess as *conceit*, but a soft self-admiration, faintly ridiculous rather than offensive.
examples: It is very often nothing but our own vanity that deceives us.
had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown

entries.definition: a person who rescues you from harm or danger
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The grandest and most urgent of the three: it names rescue from harm or danger, not the encouragement of *uncle*.

entries.definition: someone who supports or champions something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving, but the praise is for backing or speaking up for something, not for getting a person out of trouble.

entries.definition: a female person who plays a significant role (wife or mistress or girlfriend) in the life of a particular man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Defines her by her tie to one man, whether wife, mistress or girlfriend: a possessive edge *female* has none of.
examples: he was faithful to his woman
He would not hear a word said against his woman.
He came back from the sea to his woman and his children.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The *-est* ending does the work: it does not just call the person dear but sets them above everyone else.

entries.definition: a person who loves someone or is loved by someone
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Works from either side: the one who loves or the one who is loved, stating the relation rather than acting it out.
examples: The acknowledged lovers talked and laughed; the unacknowledged were silent.
these violent young lovers carry everything their own way

entries.definition: a person who founds or establishes some institution
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Deeply respectful: it makes the founder the institution's parent, giving it a family line and the founder a right to thanks.
examples: George Washington is the father of his country
He is honoured as the father of the modern hospital.
The fathers of the new school met to draw up its rules.

entries.definition: someone to whom private matters are confided
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defines the friend entirely by what you can tell them, so closeness means trusted secrets, not time spent together as with *companion*.

entries.definition: a female person who is a fellow member of a sorority or labor union or other group
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns fellow membership of a union, a sorority or any other group into a family tie between women, warmer than plain *member*.
examples: At the meeting she thanked her union sisters for their support.

entries.definition: a woman who cohabits with an important man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names her position without accusing her of breaking a marriage: she is defined by the home she shares and the man's standing.

entries.definition: an adulterous woman; a woman who has an ongoing extramarital sexual relationship with a man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blame is built into the word: a woman in an ongoing affair outside marriage, where *concubine* names only a shared household.
examples: He kept a mistress in town for years while his wife stayed in the country.

entries.definition: an old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A pet name for any old woman, grandmother or not - familiar where *mother* is respectful, and it shrinks her to her age.

entries.definition: an ugly evil-looking old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disgust and nothing more: the same ugly, evil-looking figure as *witch* but without power, so it mocks where *witch* shrinks back.

entries.definition: a term of address for an elderly woman
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Said to an old woman rather than about her, and calling her this gives her the standing of family.
examples: The soldier took the old woman's basket at the gate and said, "Let me carry this for you, Mother."

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the person themselves as something another made and can aim at any unpleasant or dishonest job, where *tool* condemns only their usefulness.
examples: He was no free man in that office, only a creature of the duke.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful, with some mockery - the person moves and acts, but the strings and the dishonesty behind it belong to whoever pulls them.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coldest of the three: the person is a thing picked up for dirty or merely unpleasant jobs, valued only for being used.

entries.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral: it says only that the person does not belong here, and allows they may belong elsewhere just as normally.
examples: After ten years in the village he was still treated as a stranger.

entries.definition: a person's reputation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest word for how others see a person, neither good nor bad itself: it takes whatever *character* or disgrace gets attached.
examples: he wanted to protect his good name
He would do nothing that might harm his good name in the town.

entries.definition: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same high respect and honor as *reputation*, said in a more formal way.

entries.definition: disgrace or shame
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the disgrace or shame as laid at someone's door, so blame is heard in it where *shame* only records the state.
examples: he brought reproach upon his family
His conduct brought reproach on the whole family.
She lived without reproach of any kind.

read_order: sorted by family so a packet carries a family's rewrites together
